answer: Memory-hard space proofs curb Sybil attacks in an AI-agent economy by binding each identity to dedicated RAM. An agent computes an identity-salted dependency trellis where each vertex hashes pseudorandom parent labels, commits the Merkle root, and answers spot openings within a tight timeout. Because recomputing missing labels exceeds the cutoff, attackers cannot run a hollow stub and must provision real DRAM per identity. Yet network jitter or high latency can falsely reject honest agents.
